_doc: VISIBLE CONDITION: MARKS (Phase 063). Each resident carries a small set of surface marks, each a level from 0 (none) to MARK_RULES.max_level. A level rises from the work or event that causes it (the `marks` rows on RECIPES and SHOCKS, MARK_HARM for each route of harm, MARK_EVENTS for other events) and falls with time (decay per day), with rain (rain_wash per day of full exposure, washable marks only), with washing (the `wash` act, MARK_RULES.wash_water and wash_drop) and with changing clothes (clothes_change_drop). Rain also wets the resident (MARK_RULES.wet_gain per day of full exposure). The world publishes the marks and never decides what an observer concludes. A mark is visible to a viewer when the viewer is within see_range cells, in light of at least see_light (0 dark, 1 full day), and the mark's level is at least visible_level. notice_skill names the trade skill a viewer needs to notice the mark at that detail (null: anyone who can see it). Phase 062's perceiver reads these as evidence; nothing in the simple village reads them. Every number is APPROX: a design choice of the right order, not a measured or sourced figure, so the seed gives none. The levels are relative scales, not physical units. Sources for the kinds of work only: charcoal burning, milling and digging are the work the recipes already name (RECIPES); their marks are the kinds of dust, sweat and mud that work leaves on a worker, which is a plain-sense judgement, not a measured figure (APPROX).
